Subject: Performance SLO qualification / cost levers — follow-up

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet you both. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth before we kick off the POC.

Summary of your targets (please correct if I mis-typed):
- Primary product: customer-facing chat with streaming responses.
- Latency targets: p95 end-to-end response latency <= 200 ms; p99 <= 350 ms. For streaming UI, first-token latency <= 250 ms, steady-state per-token latency target ~50 ms.
- Throughput / concurrency: peak concurrency ~50 simultaneous active users; average request = ~400 tokens, peak sustained throughput target ~6k tokens/sec.
- Quality tolerance: willing to accept up to ~2% drop in metric-labeling accuracy for lower cost model variants.

Key cost/performance levers we discussed: continuous batching, prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, quantization profiles (int8 / nf4), and model-variant routing (smaller quantized model for low-criticality traffic, larger model for high-quality fallback).

Ask/next steps:
1) Priyom & Dev: can you validate the numbers above and propose concrete runtime configs we should try for the POC (batch size, latency timeout, cache TTL, quantization profile recommendations)?
2) Chris/Ava: please confirm the traffic sample (15k–50k monthly active chats) and whether streaming-first-token latency is the highest priority.
3) I'll assemble a short POC plan (2-week baseline run + configuration matrix) and share a draft SOW & playbook.

Attachments: high-level notes will follow (will attach SLO notes & playbook).

Thanks,

Thanks, Marissa — quick technical follow-up with recommended starting configs for the POC and expected cost/perf tradeoffs. High-level guidance below; happy to sync with Chris/Ava for a 30-min tech call.

1) Continuous batching:
- Suggested start: max_batch_size = 64, batch_timeout_ms = 12 ms.
- Rationale: For 400-token avg requests, this yields good GPU utilization while keeping first-token latency in target range when combined with streaming.

2) Streaming and first-token latency:
- Use asynchronous prefix construction + early flush for first-token emit (first-token path prioritized). Expect first-token latencies ~150–250 ms depending on model size.

3) Caching:
- Prefix/KV cache for repeated opening prompts (TTL 6–24 hours depending on freshness).
- If 20–30% of sessions share similar prefixes, caching can reduce per-token cost by ~15–30% in practice.

4) Quantization profiles / model variants:
- Profile A (accuracy-first): float16 / large model (baseline quality).
- Profile B (cost-first): int8 / nf4 quantization on medium model variant — good cost reduction (~2–3x token-cost reduction) with expected <2% quality delta on classification/labeling tasks.
- Fallback policy: route 80% traffic to Profile B and reserve Profile A for high-confidence or downgrade-on-failure routes.

5) Autoscaling & concurrency:
- For 50 concurrent active users, provision to handle 60–70 concurrent inference contexts to account for spikes. Autoscale thresholds: scale-up at 70% GPU util, scale-down at 30%.

6) POC matrix (what we'll test):
- Baseline: large model / fp16 / no caching / small batch (16)
- Test A: medium model / int8 / prefix cache enabled / batch 64
- Test B: medium model / nf4 / more aggressive batching / cache TTL 24h

Deliverables: sample runbook + config files for the POC and rough cost estimates per million tokens for each profile. I'll attach the SLO playbook and a short config template.

--

Thanks, Marissa and Priyom — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Streaming is required; first-token latency is our highest priority since it drives perceived responsiveness in the UI.
- We expect ~15k monthly active chats to start (growth to 50k in 6 months). Peak concurrency estimate 40–60, as Marissa noted.
- A couple of operational constraints: we need predictable tail latency (p99) during sales events; if quantization increases p99 risk we may need additional fallback routing.

On cost: can you provide a ballpark comparison (per million tokens) for the three POC configs you listed (baseline / Test A / Test B)? Also curious how caching affects measured unit cost vs raw inference cost.

Finally — we'd like Redwood to run a 2-week POC using a production-like traffic replay (we can provide anonymized logs). Can we schedule the SRE/infra pairing call next week? Our time window: Tue/Wed 10am–2pm PT.

Thanks,
